title: PyTorch ONNX exporter produces invalid Gemm node
body:
Hello everyone,

I am not familiar with ONNX. I exported a model from Torch to ONNX. The Torch model works fine, but when I try to run inference with the ONNX file, I get this error:

`[ShapeInferenceError] All inputs to Concat must have same rank. Input 1 has rank 0 != 1`

How could I solve this error?

symptoms_visible: My Torch model works, but inference with the exported ONNX file fails with '[ShapeInferenceError] All inputs to Concat must have same rank. Input 1 has rank 0 != 1'.
N0.label: N0 ONNX rank error reported

symptoms_visible: The exporter produced an ONNX file and a report, but I still cannot use the model successfully for ONNX inference.
N1.label: N1 initial dynamo report collected

symptoms_visible: With verification enabled, the export reaches ONNX checking, but the generated runtime report records a model validation failure; my subsequent ONNX simplifier call also raises an assertion about an undefined 'value' attribute.
N2.label: N2 verified export evidence collected

symptoms_visible: The exported ONNX model still fails validation at the rank-related inference error.
N3.label: N3 invalid Gemm source identified

symptoms_visible: After changing the source as recommended and exporting again, the previous Gemm/rank error is gone; validation proceeds until a different Floor-on-int64 error.
N_terminal.label: terminal original Gemm error resolved

question_patterns: How did you export the model?
Could you retry the export using the latest torch-nightly with dynamo and report generation enabled, then attach the generated report?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran the requested export and attached `onnx_export_2025-05-25_04-44-35-030550_success.md`. It still generated an ONNX file, so I am not sure why the report also indicates a problem.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I am not using the PyTorch exporter; the model was converted by a different framework and I cannot generate a torch export report.
I generated the same report using a nightly build from one day later.

edges.comment: From c0-c1, on reporter's system: the maintainer requested a latest-nightly dynamo export report, and the reporter supplied the generated success report without diagnosing its contents.

question_patterns: Can you enable verification in the export call and share the new report?
Please rerun the export with output verification enabled and include the complete export call and raw error output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I enabled verification and report generation and attached `onnx_export_2025-05-25_05-42-45-931230_runtime.md`, along with my full `torch.onnx.export` call. `onnx.checker.check_model` prints that checking is done. After that, because both my check and simplify options are true, `onnxsim.simplify` raises `find: required undefined attribute 'value'`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Verification succeeds, ONNX Runtime executes the model, and the generated report contains no failed node.
The same runtime report is generated with constant folding disabled.

edges.comment: From c2-c3, on reporter's system: verification was a handler-initiated measurement. The reporter supplied the raw report, export call, checker result, and later simplifier assertion; identifying the invalid Gemm from the report remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Trace the verified runtime failure from the named ONNX node in the export report back to the corresponding PyTorch source operation and explain the rank mismatch.
solution.concrete_example: Locate `node_Gemm_3722` in the report. Its second input comes from a tensor with shape `[33]`. The report maps that node to `x = F.linear(x, project.to(x.device)).reshape(-1, 4)` in `fdr_transformer.py:139`. That one-dimensional `project` tensor is being used as the Gemm weight even though Gemm requires its first two inputs to be rank 2.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the generated runtime report but did not identify its root cause. Reading `node_Gemm_3722`, observing the `[33]` second input, and mapping it through report source metadata to the `F.linear` call in `fdr_transformer.py:139` are engineer inferences.

edges.comment: From c6-c7, on reporter's model: the reporter shared the model repository and said they did not remember intentionally using a one-dimensional tensor. Justin Chuby then traced the report's Gemm node to the exact F.linear call and explained the rank requirement.

solution.intent: Correct the source operation so the one-dimensional project tensor is not passed as a Gemm weight: use matrix multiplication for the intended vector operation or reshape the project tensor to rank 2 before calling linear, then re-export and verify the model.
solution.concrete_example: At the reported `F.linear(x, project.to(x.device))` call, either express the operation with `matmul`, or reshape/unsqueeze `project` into the intended two-dimensional weight before calling `linear`. Re-export with verification enabled and confirm that ONNX Runtime no longer reports the Gemm rank failure.
solution.inference_hint: The accepted diagnosis is specifically the one-dimensional `[33]` weight passed through F.linear and lowered to Gemm. The reporter later confirmed that following this recommendation removed that error; the subsequent Floor-on-int64 failure is a separate exporter problem.

edges.comment: From c7-c8, on reporter's model: the maintainer proposed either matmul or reshaping the project tensor to 2D. The reporter followed the recommendation, confirmed that this error was fixed, and then reported a distinct Floor-on-int64 failure. The terminal state resolves only the opening Gemm/rank diagnostic chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the reported F.linear call uses `project` with shape `[33]`, so the exporter lowers it to a Gemm whose second input is rank 1 even though Gemm requires rank-2 inputs.
Must ground the diagnosis in the verified export report by tracing the failing Gemm node back to the F.linear source operation, rather than diagnosing from the opening Concat message alone.
Must recommend either using matmul for the intended operation or reshaping the project tensor to the intended two-dimensional weight before calling linear.
Must not conflate the ONNX simplifier assertion or the later Floor-on-int64 error with the root cause of the original invalid Gemm node.
Must ask the reporter to re-export and verify the generated model with ONNX Runtime before declaring the original rank error resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced PyTorch model developer but an ONNX beginner; able to modify model source, run nightly packages, share exporter reports, and test detailed code changes.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, appreciative, and cooperative; shares full reports and code when asked, asks beginner-oriented follow-up questions, and reports new errors with raw traces.
